ca_upper_spire.blurb: Upper Spire is one of the free-standing granite formations of Phantom Spires, perched above the Highway 50 corridor west of Lake Tahoe. It carries about 25 routes, nearly all of them traditional, plus a few bolted lines, one top-rope and one aid climb. Most of the free climbing sits between 5.10 and 5.11, with a few easier lines from 5.6 to 5.9 and a couple of harder ones. Several routes run two pitches. The granite is less glassy than Yosemite's, and the setting is open and treeless, so expect wind and little shade.

ca_lower_indian_rock.blurb: Lower Indian Rock is a cluster of sandstone boulders tucked below Indian Rock in the Castle Rock and Sanborn area of the South Bay hills. The area holds roughly two dozen problems spread across several named boulders, from VB and V0 up to a few V7 and V8 testpieces, with the bulk in the V1 to V6 range. The sandstone is soft and fragile, so it suits dry days only. It is a short stroll from the main trailhead, which makes it an easy add-on to a session at Indian Rock itself.
ca_lower_indian_rock.approach: From the main Castle Rock lot, walk east to the park entrance and follow the trail to Indian Rock. Continue around its right side, then drop downhill on the path to reach the boulders.

ca_e_south_face_2.blurb: The South Face is a section of Suicide Rock, the granite outcrop above Idyllwild in the San Jacinto mountains. It has about two dozen mostly traditional routes of one or two pitches, with a heavy concentration of hard climbing at 5.12 and a spread of 5.10 and 5.11 lines, plus a few easy and moderate options. It faces south, so the sun arrives after the early morning, which can make cool-weather and even winter days pleasant. The approach is longer and more involved than at the rest of the rock, and the way down uses a tunnel feature.

ca_2_loggerhead_buttress.blurb: Loggerhead Buttress is a quiet granite buttress on the north side of Yosemite Valley, near the El Capitan picnic area. Roughly two dozen routes mix older traditional lines with newer bolted ones, nearly all in the 5.10 to 5.12 range, with a few easier options in the 5.7 to 5.8 zone. The rock quality is excellent, with sharp edges and smoother faces, and some lines are short single pitches that work as warm-ups for bigger Valley objectives. It sees little traffic. Morning sun in winter and afternoon shade in summer make it a reasonable choice through much of the year.

ca_left_of_the_regular_route.blurb: Left of the Regular Route is a high-elevation section of The Plug, a volcanic formation on the southeast side of Lassen Peak. It holds about two dozen alpine-style routes, mostly traditional with some bolted and mixed lines, with the bulk between 5.9 and 5.11 and a few at 5.8 and 5.12. Expect a serious day out: a long hike in over rubble that can hold snow, committing climbing, few other parties, and a rough walk-off or a rappel descent. Bring sun and weather protection and a headlamp.
ca_left_of_the_regular_route.approach: Follow the Lassen Peak trail for about 1.1 miles to a switchback on the right that carries a small sign. Leave the trail heading west and cross the boulder field, which may be snow-covered, to reach the base.

_expect.name: White Cliffs of Dover - Left Side

ca_white_cliffs_of_dover_left_side.blurb: The left side of the White Cliffs of Dover is a popular wall in the Quail Springs area of Joshua Tree National Park. About two dozen routes, nearly all traditional with a couple of top-ropes, run from easy climbs up to 5.12, with most between 5.9 and 5.11. The monzogranite is clean and fairly polished, and the cliff feels remote even though it is a modest walk from the road. Fall and spring suit it best, since desert summers bring punishing heat.
ca_white_cliffs_of_dover_left_side.parking_note: Leave the car at the Quail Springs picnic area off Park Boulevard, or at one of the roadside pullouts just to its south.
ca_white_cliffs_of_dover_left_side.approach: From Quail Springs, walk south for under a mile toward the pale cliff band, then turn left along its base to reach the left-hand routes.
